what_happened: The person running Athena deleted by hand the 21 GB writer build folder of job 20261102-063419-0beg, a job held on low disk that depends on the planning work. The job was held, not failed. No acceptance criterion, check or finding failed. The disk-ordering fix that would remove a job's own build before the free-space check is itself still held, so the same gap stopped the job again. This is the second hand deletion today.
cause: Athena has no disk lifecycle tied to a build's own state. The free-space guard counts a regenerable build as space the job still needs, and the step that removes that build runs after the guard. The hold only waits and reclaims nothing, so a held job's own build blocks its resume. The fix is an ordinary queued job that needs the same disk, so the bug holds its own fix. The fix has not been made urgent or exempt from the guard, even though this is the ninth or so hand cleanup. Larger builds (21 GB) make the gap worse.
prevention: Give Athena a disk lifecycle owned by the build's state. Once a producer finishes and its changes are committed, the regenerable writer build is removed before the free-space check, and the guard excludes the held job's own build from the space it requires. A held job on low disk automatically reclaims its own build and any orphaned builds of interrupted jobs, then resumes. Also make the disk-ordering fix run first and in a way that does not depend on the free disk it is meant to create, for example by having the drain reclaim builds before it admits the job.
proposed_request: Fix the disk lifecycle so a job is never held or failed on low disk because of its own regenerable build. Outcome: (1) after a producer finishes and its work is committed, its writer build folder is removed before the free-space check in the checks stage; (2) the free-space guard does not count the job's own regenerable build as space it needs; (3) when a job is held on low disk, Athena itself reclaims that job's build and the builds of interrupted or finished jobs, then resumes the job without the person running Athena action; (4) the same reclaim runs on retry and at build start, not only at drain start. Acceptance: a test with a job whose own build leaves free space under the 10 GB limit shows the build removed first and the checks stage running; a held low-disk job resumes with no hand deletion; the reclaim never removes a build that a running job still needs. Run this ahead of the other queued items, and queue it so it can start even when disk is low.
